subject: PoC path and trial success gates — deployment mode decision
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Megan Lewis <megan@clearcorps.health>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@clearcorps.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 16:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap: deployment mode options & proposed PoC approach

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the candid discussion about risk and compliance for ClearCorps' inference needs. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment for the PoC path selection.

Key constraints you called out:
- PHI in prompts and outputs (requires encryption at rest + strict key controls)
- Want to minimize cross-region traffic; primary workload stays in us-east-1
- Expected steady throughput: ~300 requests/minute with 2–3k tokens/session peak
- Procurement timeline: decision window ~6 weeks, P0 is security sign-off

Deployment mode options we covered (top-level):
1) Hosted API — fastest, low operational lift; Redwood handles KMS, but you flagged PHI constraints as the blocker unless we enable Customer-Managed KMS and dedicated model tenancy.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool in your region; stronger isolation, can meet SLA, supports customer KMS via RBAC and VPC egress controls.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — full control, on-prem option for air-gapped; longer setup and procurement overhead.

Proposed PoC approach for decisioning:
- Week 0–1: Security spike to validate KMS + audit log exports (proof that telemetry can be routed to your logging).
- Week 2–4: Trial workload run (production-like requests) against either Dedicated or Private path depending on outcome of the spike.
- Success gates: latency 95p < 300ms for interactive flows OR sustained throughput >= 250 rps for batch scoring; audit logs available in their destination; no P0 security findings.

Asks / next steps:
- Ethan: can you confirm whether procurement will accept a Dedicated deployment with Customer-Managed KMS (we can provide attestation and a network topology diagram)?
- Megan: please confirm who on your infra/security team should be included on the security spike so we can schedule the first 90-minute deep-dive.
- Ben / Karthik: I’ll need a short checklist and a draft statement of work for Dedicated vs Private pricing so procurement has something to review.

I’ve attached a short network sketch and a draft SOW stub for discussion. Happy to jump back on a quick sync — propose Tue 29 Mar 09:00 or Wed 30 Mar 14:00 ET.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ClearCorps_SOW_v1.pdf (draft), network_topology.png (sketch)
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@clearcorps.health>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Lewis <megan@clearcorps.health>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment mode options & proposed PoC approach

Monica — thanks for the recap. A couple quick clarifications from my side after reviewing with infra/security: 

1) Hosted API is a non-starter for the initial PoC unless Redwood can guarantee the keys are never in Redwood-managed KMS — we need customer KMS with an HSM-backed key and the option to rotate keys on our side.
2) Dedicated capacity looks promising if we can get:
   - A diagram showing egress flow and where logs land (we need logs sent to our Splunk instance)
   - A commitment that model versions pinned in the PoC won’t be silently upgraded without a rollback plan
3) Private (on-prem) is our long-term preference for production, but procurement will want to see a shorter-term win — if Dedicated gets us through security sign-off quickly we’ll consider mixing modes (Dedicated for trial, then Private for prod).

Timeline notes: procurement is ready to review pricing next week, but security team wants the spike (Week 0–1) to be scheduled ASAP so they can sign off. They can allocate an engineer to pair with Redwood on the spike on Mon/Tue next week.

I’ll loop procurement separately (procurement@clearcorps.health) and confirm the contact from security. We’re leaning: run the spike against Dedicated (customer-managed KMS + VPC egress) and surface any blockers.

—Ethan
Ethan Cole | Senior Infrastructure Engineer, ClearCorps Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@clearcorps.health>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Megan Lewis <megan@clearcorps.health>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment mode options & proposed PoC approach

Ethan — great, thanks for the direction. Quick notes on procurement and SOW options so your team has something to react to next week: 

- Dedicated PoC (recommended first step):
  * Reserved GPU pool in us-east-1 scoped to your namespace
  * Customer-Managed KMS is supported; Redwood will provide instructions for granting CryptoKey access and an attestation letter for HSM-backed keys
  * Pricing: two-week trial credit + discounted hourly rate while PoC runs; I’ll attach an example cost breakout in the HubSpot deal.

- Private/on-prem (prod target):
  * Longer lead time (4–8 weeks to provision & secure), includes on-site validation if required
  * Works with your existing KMS/HSM and can be air-gapped per request

Action items I’ll own for Monday:
1) Draft a short Dedicated PoC SOW that calls out the success gates Monica listed and the network/logging flows.
2) Provide a one-page pricing example (two options: 2-week evaluation credit; or 30-day reserved trial).
3) Share the rollback/upgrade policy for pinned model versions.

If you want, we can scope the PoC to a single critical flow (the claims-routing prompt set) to keep the scope tight and measurable.

Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0248
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 28 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment mode options & proposed PoC approach — confirmed next steps

Thanks all — quick confirmation and calendar invites coming your way. Per the thread we’ll proceed with the Dedicated PoC as the path of least friction for security sign-off; scope is the claims-routing prompt set as Ben suggested. Below are the mutually agreed items and owners: 

Mutual action plan (PoC) — Week 1–4
- Security spike (Week 1) — objective: validate customer-managed KMS + Splunk log export
  * Owner: Ethan (ClearCorps) + Karthik (Redwood) — schedule 90-min deep-dive this week
- PoC workload run (Week 2–4) — objective: run 10k production-like requests against Dedicated pool
  * Owner: Monica (Redwood) / ClearCorps Dev lead (tbd)
- Success gates (both must be met):
  * Observability: logs delivered to ClearCorps Splunk destination with request ID and token redaction applied
  * Performance: interactive 95p latency < 300ms OR sustained throughput >= 250 rps for the scoring flow
  * Security: no P0 findings in the spike; KMS ownership validated
Deliverables and paperwork
- Dedicated PoC SOW (Ben) — draft to procurement for review by Wed 30 Mar
- Pricing illustration (Ben) — included in SOW; two options for trial term
- Network diagram and attestation (Karthik) — posted to the related SharePoint link
Please confirm the security contact who will attend the spike and which time window works for you (Ethan mentioned Mon/Tue). I’ll send calendar invites and attach the SOW draft and topology after Ben finalizes.
Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.
Monica
